title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 5
paragraphs: As regards Sardis, then, his plan was thrown into confusion; and when Histiaeus was disappointed of this hope, the Chians attempted to restore him to Miletus at his own request. The Milesians, however, having been glad before to be rid of Aristagoras, were by no means eager to receive another tyrant into their land, having tasted freedom; and indeed, when Histiaeus tried to return to Miletus by force and under cover of night, he was wounded in the thigh by one of the Milesians. Repulsed from his own city, he returned to Chios; and from there, since he could not persuade the Chians to give him ships, he crossed over to Mytilene and tried to persuade the Lesbians to give him ships. They manned eight triremes and sailed with Histiaeus to Byzantium; and stationing themselves there, they captured the ships sailing out of the Pontus, except where the crews said they were ready to do Histiaeus's bidding.
